findings.title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks existing OAuth grant providers at startup
findings.body: `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` is a provider factory interface, and existing custom grant factories compiled against the previous version do not implement `getShortcut()`. They can still be discovered, but `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` invokes this new method for every discovered factory, causing an `AbstractMethodError` and preventing the server from starting when such a provider is installed. Preserve binary compatibility with a default method or otherwise avoid calling the new method on providers that do not implement it.

findings.title: Grant shortcut contract permits values the token decoder cannot parse
findings.body: The interface documentation permits a shortcut that is “usually like 3-letters” and the implementation does not validate its length, but `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` concatenates the entire value while `getTokenContextFromTokenId()` requires the context prefix to be exactly six characters and reads exactly two grant characters. A custom grant provider returning a three-character shortcut will issue access-token IDs which the default decoder always rejects as malformed. Require and validate exactly two-character shortcuts (including at provider initialization), or encode the context in a length/version-delimited format.

findings.title: Access-token event matcher does not validate the expected grant shortcut
findings.body: The matcher extracts `substring(3, 5)`, although the grant shortcut occupies offsets 4 and 5 in the six-character prefix, and it returns `false` when that extracted value equals the expected shortcut. Consequently IDs such as `onrtac:<uuid>` are accepted for an expected `ac` grant because the extracted value is `ta`, while an ID whose incorrectly extracted substring happens to match is rejected. The updated integration assertions therefore do not test the encoded grant type and can mask regressions; compare `substring(4, 6)` to the expected value and fail when they differ.
